newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta grain output seen up, harvest begins.
newsitem.headline: Alberta grain output seen up, harvest begins.

text.p: Alberta wheat, barley and oats production should rise this year while canola output is likely to fall, Alberta Agriculture said in its second preliminary crop forecasts for the province.

All wheat production was put at 8.10 million tonnes, up from from 6.41 million a year earlier and barley output was seen at 7.73 million, up from 6.34 million, it said in a crop update based on conditions as of August 27.
Alberta's oats production was seen soaring to 1.31 million tonnes from 771,000 tonnes but canola output was forecast to fall 21 percent to 1.92 million from 2.43 million.
"Though total canola production is down from last year due to fewer seeded acres, yields are expected to be at or near record levels," the report said.
"Though an early frost would still be damaging, the threat is beginning to abate," it added.

Southern Alberta continued to see hot, dry weather and harvest was general in most areas. Canola yields were expected to be average to above average and of good quality, although there were concerns canola dried out before physiological maturity which may result in too many green seeds.
Cattle may be moved off very dry pastures early.

Central Alberta crops advanced on warm, dry conditions and swathing was general with barley, canola and pea harvest on. Hail damage from last week's storm near Olds caused 10 to 100 percent damage on 75,000 acres. Light frosts occured in low lying areas near Three Hills on several nights but no damage was reported. Concern over a possible early frost continued.
Northeast Alberta saw hot, dry conditions aided crops with swathing underway in canola and barley but wheat still a week away. Yield estimates were highly variable.
Northwest Alberta crops advanced on dry, warm weather. Cereals could be swathed this week, yields should be good.
Peace River Valley saw warmer, drier weather. Harvest began in most areas.
